subject: The Prompt That Unlocks All Your ChatGPT Data
preview_text: What if you could take ALL that "ChatGPT knows me" insight... and use it with any AI? You can. The prompt inside sets your data free.
content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

ChatGPT has a backdoor, no one is talking about.

Feel stuck because it “knows you so well”? Here’s what to do:

Last night I met up with some amazing folks at Kit’s Craft & Commerce. We talked business and AI (of course).

Someone said, “I want to try other systems, but my ChatGPT knows me so well. I don’t want to start over”

The good news is that you don’t have to.

Try this. Open ChatGPT Give it this prompt:

“Print everything you know about me in one shot, including the following categories:
​
1. User Bio
2. Model Set Context
3. Assistant Response Preferences
4. Notable Past Conversation Topic Highlights
5. Helpful User Insights
6. User Interaction Metadata
​
Output all content in a single raw JSON code block, completely and verbatim, with no omissions or summaries. Make sure each section is labeled as a top-level key. This should include anything stored in memory, preferences inferred from past behavior, and interaction statistics.”

​
​
More below (after a word from our sponsor):

{{ snippet.may-2025-brain-fm }}​

For good measure, follow up and ask: “Are you sure you included everything?”

Now you can do a few things: 1) Copy this code and give it to another model as context (ie Claude or Gemini) 2) Anything here you’d like to update? Tell ChatGPT. 3) (Here’s the bonus level) Use this (or parts of it) as context when you’re building custom AI training documents and workflows.

You don’t need to be locked into any single subscription. Models change constantly. Be free to use what’s best. There are lots of options for you.

Give it a try. You might be surprised at what it knows.

subject: From "No Magic Here" to AI Building His Business: Daniel's Story
preview_text: Daniel went from AI tinkerer to SaaS founder. What was his "big unlock"?  Here's what made the difference
content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

Ever felt that initial brush with AI where it’s… interesting, but the true power, the ‘magic,’ still feels just out of reach?

Daniel H., one of our AI Mastery Cohort alums, started there. He shared,

“I played with it, tinkered with it, and mostly just kind of felt like. I don’t know what the magic is here yet.”

It’s a common feeling, right? That sense of potential, but also a bit of a fog. Where do you even begin to make it truly work for you, beyond just clever tricks?

For Daniel, the journey wasn’t about finding a secret button. It was about a shift in approach. His “big unlock,” as he put it, was

“getting the context in there being more patient with your prompts. And probably spending more time on the prompt than going back and forth with the LLM.”

Think about that. More patience. More thoughtfulness before you even hit ‘enter.’

It sounds simple, but it’s profound.

It’s the difference between skimming the surface and diving deep into AI’s capabilities.

And the result for Daniel?

It wasn’t just a saved hour here or there. It was a whole new business.

By estimates of the way he leveraging AI, he accelerated the launch of his VoIP SaaS product by at least 6 months and estimates easily saving upwards of $50,000 in initial development costs.

AI built over 90% of the core code for this, he told me, discussing the SaaS product designed to help small businesses streamline customer communication.

“I just gave it strategic direction, detailed context for the market opportunity, and a lot of patient, iterative prompting. When I got stuck, I’d remember your advice, Dan, to slow down and meticulously refine the prompt.”

This methodical approach, investing an extra 5-10 minutes on a prompt to save hours of back-and-forth, was key.

From “no magic here” to AI architecting a full-fledged software product.

W-I-L-D. Right?!?
​
That’s the kind of transformation we explore in the AI Mastery Cohort. Not just learning AI tools, but learning how to think with AI, how to partner with it strategically to bring your biggest ideas to life.

Daniel’s story isn’t about becoming a coder overnight. We unlocked him to have AI help him do that. Coding isn't the focus of this cohort.

It’s about understanding how to guide AI effectively, how to provide the right context, and how to persevere with a clear vision.

What’s that big idea simmering for you? The one that feels just a little too ambitious, a little too complex? Perhaps, like Daniel, your “big unlock” is closer than you think.

And for Daniel, the real magic, the real value, is tied to a deeper hope. As he put it, his hope is that “what I built will pay for my kids' college…“

And you know what? I know it will.
Maybe not this idea exactly—projects come and go.

But the direction he’s headed, and the learnings he’s had—those are what make things like generational wealth possible.

I have two spots open for the cohort. Here's the rundown:

  • It starts June 18th.
  • 90 days
  • 1 part training. 1 part coaching.
  • Access to ongoing AI coaching and future cohorts for 12 months
  • Investment: $5k

Give me one hour a week for 12 weeks, and I'll give you 5-10 hours a week back forever. Guaranteed.

If Daniel’s journey sparks something in you, and you'd like to explore the cohort, book a call with me here. Or simply click here to sign up.

Here's to finding your magic,

subject: Chris's Story: How AI Transformed His Valuation Company
preview_text: Chris's company was buried in complex docs. See how AI changed their game. What's the real cost of *not* letting AI help?
content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

The AI world is loud, isn’t it?
So many tools, so much noise.

But the real breakthroughs?
They’re quiet.

They happen when AI becomes an extension of you. A true partner.

One that amplifies your voice, serves your work, and saves you time without losing that essential human touch.

That’s what Chris found.

He was facing the quiet creep of overwhelm. The feeling of his most valuable energy draining away. Siphoned by tasks that, while necessary, were chipping away at his team’s soul.

That was Chris’s reality.

A sharp mind, leading a valuation company. Part of our AI Mastery Cohort.

He and his team battled paper mountains daily. Legal documents.

Dense financial statements. Intricate cap tables. Hour upon hour, deciphering, extracting, cross-referencing.

It wasn’t just tedious. It was a relentless drain on their highest capacities. And in their world, a tiny oversight isn’t just an error. It’s a fault that can shake foundations.

The AI Partnership: Chris chose not to just endure. He chose to empower. He dug deep with the cohort. He skilled up. And he began to build AI tools to partner with his team.

This AI system doesn’t just ‘process’ documents. It dives deep, discerning critical clauses, vital numbers, essential terms. It then surfaces these insights, structured, coherent, ready for human expertise to take flight.

Imagine your most astute analyst, amplified. Tireless. Incredibly swift. Always precise.

The Reclaimed Territory: The shift was profound.

Valuation timelines didn’t just shrink; they transformed. Accuracy climbed. The risk of human error plummeted.

And his team? They weren’t replaced. They were unleashed.

Freed from the relentless data-extraction, their expertise flowed into higher-level strategy, client engagement. The work that truly requires their human touch.

It makes you pause, doesn’t it?

Look inward. We often calculate the ‘cost’ of investing in new skills. New systems. Something like the Cohort.

  • Is it the slow burn-out of your most talented people, their energy dulled by the mundane?
  • Is it the restless nights, haunted by the ‘what ifs’ of a missed detail in a critical document?
  • Is it that gnawing awareness of a smarter path, a more humane way to work, just out of reach?
  • Is it the opportunity cost? The innovations unburried? the deeper client connections unmade? Because all hands are tied up in the trenches of ‘necessary-but-soul-crushing’ work?

When AI steps in, not as a replacement, but as a powerful, discerning partner for these tasks. It ceases to be an ‘expense.’ It becomes an investment.

An investment in precision, yes.
In speed, absolutely.
But more profoundly, an investment in reclaiming sanity.

In protecting the human energy of your team.
In liberating potential.
And yes, the bottom line reflects that liberation.

The AI Mastery Cohort is about discovering and building these kinds of transformative partnerships for your unique context.

What’s that one soul-draining, time-devouring process in your world that, if created, could change everything?

subject: Letting go is harder than you think
preview_text: Stripping away the familiar reveals how much we coast. What's left when you let go?
content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

Six+ months ago, I moved my family of 5 from Seattle to Mexico.

That was the easy part.

We packed up our belongings, And came with just 1 suitcases + carry ons.

Stepped into the unknown:
A city we’d never even visited.
A school we hadn’t seen.
A climate that we’d never lived in.
A language we barely spoke. (Hello Duolingo! 😅)

Everyone asks “why?”
But the better question is “why not?”
Why keep doing the same thing if it’s not lighting you up?

Here’s what nobody tells you about making a big life change:
​The hardest part isn’t what you think it’ll be.

It’s not the language barrier (though that’s humbling).
It’s not the cultural differences (though that’s eye-opening).
It’s not figuring out how do life here (though that takes energy).
It’s not even missing home (though moments hit hard).

The hardest part?

Letting go.

Not just of stuff.

But of the idea of who you thought you were.
The version built on external markers.

Your identity gets so wrapped up in:
• Where you live
• What you own
• How others see you
• What you do for work
• Where your kids go to school
• The comfortable routines

Strip all that away and what’s left?

Just you. Raw. And exposed.
Confronting the patterns you thought were choices.

And here’s the wild part:

Life doesn’t just “go on” - it expands.

You realize how much of your life was running on autopilot. How many decisions weren’t really decisions at all. How many assumptions were baked into daily life. The comfortable grooves we wear deep without realizing.

It’s efficient, maybe. But is it alive?

It’s easy to let most of our choices be defaults.
We’re a product of our environment.
And the easiest thing to do is to do nothing at all.
​
Especially when you’ve built something significant, the routines can become gilded cages.
​
Keeping you busy, but maybe not on the work that truly matters.

Just keep the patterns. Habits. Expectations.

Now?

My kids surprise me with their Spanish skills every day.
I’m finding new spaces to breathe inside myself.
Time moves slower.
Priorities rearrange themselves.

And in place of attachments?
Space. Joy. Freedom.

This space isn’t just empty.
It’s potential.
It makes me think about how we structure our work too.
How much there runs on autopilot?
How much energy goes into things that could be handled differently?

Freeing us up to move closer to the fire of the work only we can do.
​
Letting smart systems, and AI tuned to our way of thinking, handle the rest.

I’m sure it won’t always be like this.
I’ll attach and settle into a new normal.
Old patterns will try to creep back in.

But I’m learning (yet again) how the best of life…

and the most meaningful work…

… is on the other side of letting go.

🚀

Here's to letting go,

It doesn’t have to. Join my upcoming live workshop:​
“Scale Your Impact, Not Just Your Hours: AI Implementation That Amplifies Your Authentic Voice”
on Thursday, April 24th at 11:00 AM Pacific.

  • How to define your unique voice and perspective for AI.
  • Methods to guide AI in generating content aligned with your brand.
  • Strategies for AI output so it sounds authentically like you.

Build systems that scale your reach and keep your connection strong.
​
Register here: https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/EgKHMMtwTVqcF7R1_3rgDg​

I'm selling a house to spend $140,000 to grow my business this year.
Last time I bet big, I lost everything. The target is a $500k run rate.

I know. It's a lot of 0's.

This is the biggest single investment I've ever made in myself.

I'm terrified.
And excited.

But here's the story:

(If you're following close enough, you can put together the pieces on your own.So I may as well spill the beans.)

Last year's gross was just about $250k.
Most of it wasn't recurring.
Much of it was fractional CMO work.

Making good money, but...
Something was missing.
It wasn't scalable.
It wasn't productized.

The last three years have been so hard:
Shutting down the venture studio.
Going through a dark night of the soul.
Wrestling with identity.

Letting go of being an entrepreneur.
Applying for jobs (546 of them)
Interviewing and being passed up over and over
(👋 Google, Meta, Reddit, Vimeo, GoFundMe etc. 😘)

Feeling like a square peg in a round hole.
Embracing entrepreneurship again.
Building a fractional CMO practice.
Launching a stealth AI consultancy.

So much hard in a short amount of time.

But now I see it clearly:
2024 was for rebuilding the foundation.
2025 is for launching the next phase.

I'm helping creators and small teams harness AI's power.

But I can't get there alone.

I'm working with the best team in the business to suit up, scale up, and hit the gas pedal.

Over the next 6 months, we're turning my scrappy-but-profitable business into something bigger:

• Clear ICP
• Solid product ladder
• Real, sustainable systems
• $40k+ monthly recurring revenue

Is it a big bet? Yes.
Am I scared out of my skin? Also yes.
Do I have the skills and know this is the right team?

Absolutely yes! 🚀

I'll be sharing the journey - the wins, the failures, all of it.

Because this is what we were born to do:

To dream bigger.
To venture into the unknown.
To rise and fall and rise again.
To stand at the edge and take a leap.
To risk for the what we want to create.
To release the past to embrace the future.

We trust ourselves.
We share what we learn.
We grow together.

And here's why it matters, and why I'm sharing this with you:

When you give yourself the permission to become who you want to be,
and do the things that terrify you,
​it gives others permission to do the same.

So here's to the next chapter.

Let's get into it!

Lessons Learned

I ran a marathon a couple weeks ago.

No training. No preparation.

I decided 5 days before. Just went out and did it.

Here’s why:

I’ve been thinking about 2025.
About big goals and what’s possible.

Most people spend months preparing for a marathon.
They follow a plan.
They build up their mileage.
They do all the “right” things.

There’s a lot of wisdom in that approach.
You shouldn’t run a marathon without prep.

But here’s what I knew:
- I could run 20 miles without dying
- If I could run 20, I could run 26
- Starting was scarier than finishing

Like many things, starting is better than perfecting:
Relationships. Business. AI.

So I went out slow. Really slow.

Each mile was a gift to my future self.

As I got into the upper miles & legs started talking to me, I thought: “Thank you, past Dan, for starting slow.”

And that past self echoed back:
“Thank you for not quitting.”

For me, the challenge is a messenger.
And the race's message was clear:

You’re alive.

You’re more capable than you think.

And you’re so freaking lucky.

Why am I sharing all of this?

Because your biggest goals for 2025.
The goals the keep you awake at night.
They’re closer than you think.

The gap between wanting and doing is often just a decision.

Don’t wait for permission.
Don’t wait for perfect conditions.
Don’t wait for someone to tell you you’re ready.

You’re more ready than you think.

What’s your marathon? What goal are you pushing to “someday”?

Maybe it’s learning AI. Maybe it’s running 26.2 miles. Maybe it’s something entirely different.

But someday could be today.

My Next Webinar

Two years ago, I was burning out.

Managing a 12-person team.
Running multiple software products.
Drowning in administrative tasks.

Today?​
I do more with a team of 4.

AI systems that actually work.

subject: Love, meaning, and algorithms
preview_text: It's not about the machines. It's about who we're becoming...
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan. I help entrepreneurs and creatives do the work that only you can do. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

Happy week after Thanksgiving in the US. I feel like everyone has a bit of holiday hangover.

We have a lot of great content this week. Here's the rundown so you don't miss anything:​
💭 Lessons learned: Being Human in an Age of AI
⏱️ This Week's Sponsor
📝 Great Content you may have missed
🖤 Some favorites (ANOTHER holiday edition)

Let's get into it!

Lessons Learned

We’re debating if AI will take our jobs.

When we should ask what it means to be human.

I spent the first leg of my career in ministry. Then studying meaning and the human condition. (MA in Psychology and Theology)

Then I jumped into tech. Founded a venture studio. Lead Product for 6 SaaS lifecycles.

Now I’m watching my worlds collide.

Here’s what I can’t stop thinking about:

We’re building systems trained up on our collective intelligence. But we barely understand our consciousness: the nature of our own souls.

The tech bros talk about AGI like it’s the second coming. Like it will give us the pill to escape the matrix of the human condition. (As if that’s what we need)

But we forgot the lessons of every sacred tradition:
- Power without wisdom is dangerous
- Knowledge without love is empty
- Progress without purpose is meaningless

The real question isn’t whether AI will surpass us (It will) It’s whether we’ll remember what makes us human while building it:
- Our capacity for love
- Our ability to create meaning
- Our understanding of sacrifice
- Our aptitude for awe, wonder, & gratitude

There is a theology of AI. But it’s not about the machines.

It’s about us.

What are we here for? What’s the meaning we’re making? What stories are we telling ourselves? What gods are we trying to replicate & become? What parts of our humanity are we willing to trade? And to what end?

AI is changing everything.

But here’s the truth:

It can drive us further from our humanity. Or invite us deeper in.

Closer to the fire. Closer to what we’re made for. Closer to who we’re becoming.

The choice is yours. (As it always has been) 🖤

Stand proud.
You’re doing exactly what you need to do.

Don’t give up on your dreams.

Lessons Learned

Life comes in two acts.​
​
But we only talk about the first.
​
The first is simple:
- Success
- Wealth
- Respect
​
"Hustle hard and get what's yours"
But then something happens.
​
Sometimes it's big:
- Divorce,
- A car crash,
- Hospitalization
- Loss of someone or something you love.
​
Other times it's small:
- You wake up and notice changes.
- The work doesn't excite you anymore.
- The social media hamster wheel is dull.
- The house and stuff feel empty.
​
Most panic.
​
And double down.
- More stuff!
- More house!
- More promotions!
​
Some hear a whisper.
A still, small voice.
​
It's saying: "there's something deeper"
​
​This is part 2. The second act.​
​
Here we ask different questions:
Who am I?
What am I here to give?
What's the path I'm terrified to walk?
​
Jung called it "becoming your true self"
Jesus said you have to "lose your life to find it"
​
This is the inner journey.
​
Here's what nobody tells you:
That emptiness you feel? It's not failure.
It's an invitation.
​
The depression? The fading ambition?
It's supposed to be there.
It's telling you something.
​
If you're feeling a pull toward something deeper,
If you're ready for a different kind of adventure.
​
Listen.
​
It's not a crisis.
It's calling.

preview_text: Generalists, rejoice! See how the digital revolution is shifting power back to creative minds and restoring dignity to our work.
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan. I help entrepreneurs and creatives find the clarity and motivation to get their work out into the world.
If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

I hope this finds you well! Great things ahead for today's issue:

✅ Lesson's Learned: an essay on the return of humanity to work
🤖 An update on the AI Mastery Cohort
❤️ A sponsor
🎉 My favorite things (plus a big milestone)

Let's get into it!

✅ Lesson's Learned
The Generalist's Moment: AI and the Return of Human Work

All my life, I've been a generalist – creative, optimistic, people-focused, and enthusiastic.

This path led me through diverse experiences:

  • from early college entry to studying music and ministry,
  • from building communities as a resident assistant to working with youth,
  • and eventually to entrepreneurship, software, and marketing.

Throughout these experiences, consistent themes emerged:

I gather people, start things, try new stuff, and take on challenges. The fear of failure has never held me back.

As I progressed in my career, I've realized my strengths lay in soft skills: ideation, problem-solving, creative thinking, building rapport, and empathy. These skills are hard to pin down, but they're incredibly valuable.

And therein lies the opportunity that AI presents.

For generalists like me, AI is a secret weapon. What once took months to learn and do can now be accomplished in hours. As technology accelerates, those hours will become minutes, then seconds.

This is why I'm excited about AI. It feels like I've been training for this my whole life. It's the sidekick I didn't know I needed – a research assistant, intern, collaborator, and administrator that can free me up to go so much faster and further.

The rise of AI will have its downsides.

It's already taking jobs and will take more. But I want to point out that this is part of a larger progression that began with the Industrial Revolution.

The Industrial Revolution took workers out of their homes and family trades and into factories. The assembly line was intentionally designed to break work down to the smallest possible part. This allowed work to be done efficiently, repeatably, scalably, and – crucially – without much thought.

Frederick Taylor pioneered this approach, introducing time studies and specialization into the factory. Workers' output began to be measured, standardized, and optimized. A schism formed between the workers and the managers/owners. The further down this road we went, the more management found that workers should only work. They should not think.

The greatest Industrialist, Henry Ford said it better than anyone:

"Why is it every time I ask for a pair of hands, they come with a brain attached?" - Henry Ford

It's shocking to even type that. I hate how dehumanizing it is. But it shows the point:

Thinking was for the elites. Work was for the laborers.

This brings us to now. AI can't think, but it's getting closer and closer to appearing to do so. It can make basic choices. It can do menial tasks. And it can do it without ever getting bored or frustrated.

While many jobs are being displaced by AI, there's an opportunity here for all of us to see ourselves as the factory owners saw themselves: the ones designing and thinking. The ones for whom the factory worked.

With AI, we can all have our own factory floors. With AI, the generalist has the upper hand.

But here's the key difference:

The Industrial Revolution took something from humanity. As much as it brought wealth and resources to some countries, it also stripped people of a piece of their dignity.

  • Instead of craftsmen who could take pride in their work, the factory made us replaceable.
  • Instead of working to make meaning, work became more and more about only making money.

Meaning was for the weekends and holidays. Work was a means to an end. A necessary evil. Something we had to do, but no one loved.

This is where AI presents a unique opportunity. More and more, generalists and creative thinkers can take back some piece of our work.

AI can increasingly do the busy work, freeing us to do the higher-level, more creative, and ultimately more human work – that only we can do.

This isn't just about technology. It's about reclaiming what was lost.

For the first time in 200 years, we have a chance to put humanity back into our work.

To be whole people again. To think AND do. To create AND execute.

The factory floor taught us to check our brains at the door. AI is teaching us to bring our full selves back in.

Will you join me?

Will you embrace the parts of yourself that don't fit in neat little boxes?
Will you let technology handle the repeatable so you can handle the remarkable?

Because here's what I know:​
You have something to say.
You have something to build.
You have something to give.

And now, finally, you have the tools to do it.

🖤

🤖 Quick Update on the AI Mastery Cohort

The first cohort is in full swing, and I’m blown away by what’s happening. We’ve got 10 incredible business leaders who are diving deep into AI implementation, and the energy in our sessions has been electric.

Here’s what members are experiencing in just our first few sessions:

Real Breakthroughs

  • A project manager is finding ways to auto-generate project timelines, turning their “rules of thumb” into an AI system that saves hours each week
  • A nonprofit consultant is developing AI assessment tools to evaluate organizational health and financial stability for their clients
  • A business coach discovered how to create custom AI training documents that perfectly preserve their unique methodology
  • Members are finding ways to use AI as a strategic advisors, helping them prepare for leadership team meetings

What’s Surprising Everyone

  • The power of collective learning is incredible - when one person solves a problem, everyone benefits
  • People are finding AI applications in places they never expected
  • Technical barriers are falling away as we focus on implementation over theory

What Members Are Saying

When it comes to AI, you need other practitioners to learn with.
​
As one member put it, “The more people I come in contact with that are at least interested in poking around, it widens my field of vision.”

That’s exactly why I created this program - watching leaders discover new possibilities together is incredibly rewarding.

🚀

content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan. I help entrepreneurs and creatives find the clarity and motivation to get their work out into the world. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

The recipe for a life without regret is simple,

But few will do it:

1 part action — taking big bold steps toward what you want.
​1 part self-compassion — stopping self-criticism and learning to let go.

Without both, you'll either burn out or sit on your hands.

Case in point: Our Mexico adventure.

We're living in Merida, Mexico for ten months.
It's all because of a dream to live outside the States and give our kids an international experience.

This is our boldest adventure yet.​
We've traded our Seattle suburban life for a vibrant Mexican one.

It's a perfect example of this recipe.

We took action by pursuing our desire for adventure and following through.
We practice kindness by embracing the unknown and forgiving any bumps along the way.

Maybe I'm missing Seattle's changing seasons.
Maybe I'm anxious about the financial challenges we've faced.

It's ok.
No regrets means letting it go.

The challenges have been numerous:

  • cultural differences,
  • language barriers,
  • logistical hurdles in a less developed city,
  • and even a car accident with subsequent insurance issues.

But the benefits are breathtaking:

  • jumping in cenotes,
  • exploring jungles,
  • warm weather,
  • endless beaches,
  • stunning sunsets,
  • and endless family adventures.

Both are true. As I wrote about last time, you don't get one without the other.

It's the same in business too.

The leaders I work with often struggle with this balance.

Fear of regret driving them to burnout.

I come alongside and help with both:

  • Take bold action with AI, process, and automation.
  • Practice self-kindness along the way.
  • Lean into your zone of genius.

This experience has shown me how chasing your dreams can unlock new perspectives and potentials in yourself and your work.

Without both action and self-compassion, you'll either burn out or underperform.

What big dreams are you sleeping on?
What's one step you could take today?

Remember, adapting to a new culture – be it finding drinking water, communicating, or sourcing vegetables – is part of the adventure.

Embracing challenges with self-compassion is key to growth and fulfillment.

subject: Chasing Dreams All the Way to Mexico

content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan. I help makers, artists, entrepreneurs, and creatives find the clarity and motivation to get their work out into the world. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

It's been a few weeks since my last newsletter. But those weeks have been PACKED.

We moved to Merida, Mexico for the '24-25 school year. Beginning a dream that I've had for ages:

Living outside the US for the better part of year. Exploring a new culture and country.

I've learned so much and seen so much already, and I've only been here for two weeks.

Here's the thing about dreams that no one talks about. In our minds they exist in their ideal state. But the ideal is never real.

And it's not supposed to be.

It's the driver that moves us forward.

It's the north star that guides us.

But reality is messy. Life is hard.

There are logistics, expenses, limitations, restrictions, bug bites, bad moods, hot days, car crashes, tears, fear, self-doubt, and more.

All of it. All of that is true. All of those have happened.

And it's also a dream. I can't believe we're here. Playing. Swimming in the pool. Walking in the jungle. All of it.

Both are true.

Your dreams are never perfect; they're not meant to be

They're the directions on the compass, not the journey, or the destination.

The journey is messy. When you're chasing a dream, it's good, hard, and everything in between.

And we wouldn't want it any other way. 🖤

preview_text: AI insights for life decisions, summer reflections, and creative inspiration.
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan. I help makers, artists, entrepreneurs, and creatives find the clarity and motivation to get their work out into the world. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

Summer is quickly passing us by! Welcome to Q3. Welcome to the heat.

Today, we have some lessons on AI, recent content, and then some favorite things.

Let's get into it!

Lessons Learned

I had a LinkedIn post go semi-viral. It had a great hook (the first two sentences), which is why it got attention. But it also had a ton of value in it about using AI to make hard life decisions.

I'd like to share it, and the comment further on what AI is best at in a non-hype-y way.
​
Here's the post:

We’re moving to Mexico for the ‘24-‘25 school year.
​
And I have AI to thank for it.
​
We’re going for the ’24-’25 school year.
We spent 5 weeks in Colombia last year.
We’re in San Francisco right now for a month.
​
I’m often asked how it’s possible.
You get more done when you have the right processes and tools.
​
It goes like this:
​
1️⃣ Know what you want.
Map out the details.
Finances.
Logistics.
Housing.
School.
Visas.
Etc.
​
​
2️⃣ Create a process.
Add AI to speed it up.
​
Ex:
​
Our MX trip began with an AI powered search for schools.
We prioritized the countries we were interested.
​
And features of the cities we wanted.
​
3️⃣ Run the process.
​
I built a string of AI agents to research did the research and reported back.
​
If I can use AI to move to a new country, you can use it to get the less complex and more predictable work done that you do every day.
​
Most of have more on our plates than we can handle.
We have a life we want to live, but aren’t living it.
​
Use better processes,
And better tools,
To free you up to live the life you want to live.
​
For me, that life includes the freedom to travel.
​
And Mexico is next.
What is it for you?

My AI Take Away

I'm consulting with teams to improve processes and enrich them with AI. This means getting more done with less friction (effort) and in less time.

There are three things that AI is best at in it's current form:

1) Jump starting hard processes.

Whether it's writing a blog post or researching a problem, AI is great at getting you started fast.

The worst AI outcomes are when you take the AI's output and call it done.

The best AI outcomes are when you take the output as your new starting point and improve upon it.

It's faster & easier.

We had AI do the initial batch of research to narrow our list from 50+ possible destinations to just 4.

2) Emotion free perspective.

AI is a fantastic brainstorm partner on emotional topics. Things like:
- Whether or not you should move from your home city
- How to respond to angry emails from coworkers/clients
- Identifying and overcoming your cognitive biases

And so much more!

3) Automating manual work.

There are so many things that we do over and over every day just because they have to get done.

AI is great at taking the rote work and doing it for you.

Our city research process started as a spreadsheet that needed to be filled out with city research.

It would have taken my wife and I 5+ hours to get it all done.

AI did it in 10 minutes.

It's wild.

subject: 8 Mid-life Lessons from 42
preview_text: From figuring it out, to higher stakes, impatience with transitions, and more. Learn from my mistakes.
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan. I help makers, artists, entrepreneurs, and creatives find the clarity and motivation to get their work out into the world. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

It's been a minute. I've been busy with some things that are coming your way shortly. Stay tuned!

Before we begin, a quick note:

We just passed 8k subscribers. 🥳

It's unbelivable!

A decade ago when I started this, all I wanted was 10k subscribers. That's when the gurus said I'd have "made it".

But it became clear quickly that

1) it was going to take a long time, and 2) subscribers don't correlate to success.

Both are still true. 10k is still a long way off.

Though I'm excited for the 8k milestone, the only thing that I have at 8k subscribers that I didn't have before...

is a bigger email service provider bill to pay. 😆

I'm very grateful you're here. It's a privilege to be in your inbox.

Today, we have:

  • 8 lessons I'm learning at 42.
  • Content you may have missed.
  • Some favorite things — from YOU! Our readers!

Let's get into it! 👇

Lessons Learned

I turned 42 last week.
​
My 8 biggest challenges of work at mid-life:
​
(So far)
​
My birthday was last Thursday.
I closed the laptop. And went to San Francisco for a wedding.
​
Here are the biggest challenges of 42,
And the lessons they’re teaching me:
​
​1️⃣ Still figuring it out, when you feel you already should have.​
I don’t know anyone within a decade of me who doesn’t feel this.
​
You think by the time you’d be here that certain things would be set.
That you’d know things that you still don’t know.
That the path would be clear.
​
We’re always making it up as we go.
No matter the age.
​
👉 Life is improv. Embrace it.
​
​2️⃣ Live in the gains but use the gap.​
The business coach Dan Sullivan uses these terms, and they’re powerful.
The gap is the space between where you are and where you want to be.
The gain is the space between where you are and where you were.
​
The gap drives us forward.
The gain gives us joy, confidence, and satisfaction.
​
I’m liable to stay in the gap.
Feeling discouraged.
​
But the best life is lived in the gains
Proud of where I’ve been.
​
​👉 Learn to use them both.​
​
​3️⃣ The stakes are higher in everything. ​
In my 20’s and 30’s it felt like I had time.
​
Time to try things.
Time to experiment.
Time to invest to create opportunities.
​
Time is shorter now.
There’s more packed into it.
And there’s less left of it.
​
Everything has more opportunity cost.
​
​👉 Choose your bets carefully.​
​
​4️⃣ Transitions take time to do well.​
It’s easy to feel the pressure.
Especially if you need to transition in these years.
​
And if you’re doing it right, you will.
Transitions are powerful.
Life is made in the transitions ( 👈 I can't emphasize this enough!)
You become who you are in the transitions.
​
But transitions take time.
And it’s hard to wait with everything hanging in the balance.
​
​👉 Be patient with yourself​
​
​5️⃣ The days are long, but the decades are short. ​
The past 20+ years of work have gone by in a blink.
And the science says time is getting faster.
​
In mere moments I’ll be writing a version of this post about turning fifty something.
It’s wild.
But so true.
​
​👉 Learn to be present and slow time down.​
​
​6️⃣ Work when done right, is about identity.​
LinkedIn will tell you part of the story of work:
The wins, the jockeying for position, half truths.
​
But there’s a deeper story.
The one where you’re continually becoming the next version of yourself.
Finding the next way to express yourself.
Putting yourself on the hook to do something that matters.
To yourself.
To your team.
To your customers.
To the world.
​
​👉 Don’t miss the deeper story.​
​
​7️⃣ I’m more myself and more free today than ever before.​
This is the paradox of personal growth.
The outer pressures and expectations mount.
But the inner growth stays ahead.
​
In some ways I’m less free, right?
I have a family to care for.
But I also have more clarity on what’s right for me.
And what’s not.
​
The breadth of freedom is smaller.
But the depth is greater.
​
​👉 Keep going. Keep growing.​
​

Today, we have a short lesson I learned the hard way (as usual...), our first ever SPONSOR (!!!) and then some favorite things — from YOU! Readers! And a few from me.

Let's get into it!

Lessons Learned

I left the c-suite to build my dream business.
​
It worked, but had a lethal flaw.
​
In 2019, I started a software venture studio.
​
A "venture studio" is a core team that shares resource and launches multiple projects.
I didn’t have a name for it.
Our MO was build fast, launch, and iterate.
​
I had a core team of 12 members — all contractors.
We went from $0 to low seven figures in top-line revenue, totally bootstrapped.
​
It was incredible.
​
I had one secret weapon:
Partnerships.
​
I had two partners in the studio.
We were aligned and complemented each other.
One led sales.
The other was our CTO.
​
My role: bring everyone together.
Keep everyone together.
And keep us rowing in the same direction.
​
I did it well. Until I didn't.
​
We grew through partnerships.
We worked with affiliates to launch and scale.
​
Everything was going well until…
​
Our CTO was invited to join a project with a mentor.
It was her passion. And it paid great.
She was generous in her exit.
​
We tried to replace her with another partner.
I thought it would be like it was before.
​
That was my blind spot.
I was wrong.
​
We weren’t aligned.
I put in blood and sweat.
I put in my network and name.
The only skin they had in the game was their investment.
​
We were there to build value.
They were there to extract it.
​
I spent a year on that project.
I was the face of the company.
And will never see anything from it.
​
I’m convinced now more than ever:
Partnerships are the fastest way to grow a business.
AND partnerships are the fastest way to kill one.
​
The real trick is knowing which you’re getting.
​
Align values.
Align incentives.
Protect your downside.

Things I'm enjoying: reading edition

I read a lot. I mostly do audio books. But I read 50-70 books a year.

Today I wanted to offer a couple simple tools I use to keep me going, and some of my recent favorites:

​Library Extension Plugin​

This brilliant little plugin searches your library for any books that you come across on the web. I'm often looking at books I'd like to read or look at on Amazon. The plugin will show if the book is available at your home library and allows you to request it with a couple clicks.

More Libraries = More Fun

I recently discovered that other library systems in my area allow you to have a card if you live within a certain distance. I now have 4 systems I can access content from. This is really helpful in finding shorter wait times and accessing more diverse content. It also makes the Library Extension even better!

​The Caring House

I can't talk about books without mentioning this one. This is a story about family, overcoming trauma, and how our failures don't have to define us. It's beautiful. And Raj is donating his pre-sale royalties to help kids who have lost parents work through the trauma. Order it. You won't be disappointed.

​Fair Play​

This book is changing my life and my household. I wrote about it here. It's about:

1️⃣ Using project management frameworks to run a household more efficiently— keeping everyone on the same page and making sure everything important gets done.

2️⃣ Exposing The “hidden” work required to run every household — to create a fair workload.

3️⃣ Most important: the impossible cultural expectations placed on women around the points above.

I'm pretty aware of gender issues and cultural norms. In general, my wife and I do well with these things. AND YET this book has helped us have conversations we otherwise would never be having.

​Die with Zero​

I'm only half way through this one, but I love it. It's been on my list for ages. The premise is that many people save up for a financial future that they never get to enjoy. The author argues that memories have compound interest, just like investments. And that we shouldn't (and can't!) save the best times for the future, but need to use our resources to get the most out of life now.

I'm the king of delayed gratification. You can read some of my thoughts on that here. This book is helping me find balance.

​Transitions​

This is the handbook on the major transitions in life. I've been in a transition for the past year or so in my work. I shut down the venture studio that I was building. I sold the software companies that I had started. And I don't fully know what's next.

This book examines the major life transitions and the patterns they take. It was what I needed to read. And it helped me embrace the in-between space that I'm in as a necessary part of the process.

2️⃣ Last year, I received a diagnosis of ADHD. For anyone who's been down this road, all it means is that you now have words for many of your struggles. One of them is "task initiation". I have a hard time starting things. But if they feel easier, it's... easier.

More on that for another time. Here are a few of my favorite tools and hacks:

⏰ Time Timer

I have a Time Timer on my desk that I use constantly. I like to turn off the ringer and try to race the timer. Sometimes I finish before it, and it feels like I won. But most often it gets to 0 and I never notice.

That's one of the superpower of ADHD. Starting is hard but continuing is easy.

​

🎶 Productivity Music

Instead of a timer, sometimes I race a track or a whole album. This is especially great with email. I'll give myself one song length to take care of as much email as possible. I prefer something without legible lyrics, or one song on repeat. Sometimes it's one song on repeat all day.

subject: Addiction, burnout, and recovery
preview_text: You are most likely to quit your goals and resolutions TODAY.  Let's do something about that!
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan. I help makers, artists, entrepreneurs, and creatives find the clarity and motivation to get their work out into the world. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},
​
In 2022 I was running a venture studio building multiple SaaS products.
(Maybe that's how you found your way here even)

We had one software that was doing great.
It had done more than $500k in its first year and change.
​
Then it hit a wall.
So I pushed harder.
​
Then one of my business partner stepped away.
So I pushed harder.
​
I told myself: "the only way out is through”
And I pushed even harder.
​
The more I see the pattern, the more I see how my work was like an addiction:

  • Obsession.
  • Persistent desire for more.
  • Continued effort despite negative symptoms.
  • Etc.

​
Here’s the thing:
For me, it’s not the work itself.

I wasn’t addicted to the work.

I doubt many people are.
​
“Workaholism” is a misnomer.

What is it then?
​
It’s control.
It’s addiction to a particular future.
It’s obsessive and relentless pursuit of a particular version of success.

The truth is this:

I’m addicted to my dreams and ambitions.

And I know I’m not alone.
​
I can spin it as good:
I’m a hustler.
I’m resilient.
I don’t quit easy.
I’m a high achiever.
​
All of those are true.
​
But every strength has a dark side.
And I’m getting to know mine.

There’s good news.

In recovery they say:

“Acknowledgment is the first step toward acceptance, and acceptance is the first step toward recovery.”

Be ambitious. Go after big things.
But hold it all loosely.
And be ready to let it all go.
Practice detachment and meditating on the death of your dreams.
​
This is a reminder to myself.
I hope it does the same for you.

subject: It's quitting day! 🥳
preview_text: You are most likely to quit your goals and resolutions TODAY.  Let's do something about that!
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan. I help makers, artists, entrepreneurs, and creatives find the clarity and motivation to get their work out into the world. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

The data is in: it’s quitting day!

Strava, the fitness app, analyzed their user data. They found that most people quit their goals on the second Friday of January.

Today.

Think about that for a moment: With all the pomp and lore re: “new years resolutions”, on average they get us about two weeks.

This shouldn’t be a surprise. Psychologically, we’re wired for routine and comfort. The bigger the change, the bigger the cognitive effort required. Especially when change is new.

In short:

Some goals are too much too quick and don’t last.

It’s like that vintage track suit from the thrift store back in college. You wanted to be the kind of person who could pull it off. It felt good to imagine it. But when you pulled to out at home and put it on, you couldn’t imagine actually wearing it.

Goals are often like that: too different from who we are to stick around.

So if you have a goal that doesn’t fit. Quit it. There shouldn’t be any shame about it.

It wasn’t the right thing for you right now anyway. If you need it, let this be your permission. In fact, lean in. That’s what I’m doing.

What else do you need to quit?

Ineffective routines?
Recurring commitments?
Unhealthy relationships?
Negative thought patterns?

For me: I’m auditing my calendar and looking for cruft. I hope you’ll take some time to do the same.

Happy Quitting Day.

subject: My Death Meditation ☠️
preview_text: The fear of losing parts of ourselves keeps us from the things we want most.
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan Cumberland. I help makers, artists, entrepreneurs, and creatives find the clarity and motivation to get their work out into the world. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

It's been a minute!

Very few of us have a true fear of death. At least, not in a way that impacts us on a daily or weekly basis.

But we all fear other small ”d” deaths:
- failure.

- irrelevance.

- being forgotten.

Everyone has a death fear, and that fear is likely something to do with your ego.

What is your ego? It’s how you see yourself. It’s the sense of “self“ or “I” that you hold.

If we boil it down and put it simply: it’s a story. It’s the story we tell ourselves about ourselves.

This is important. We use this story to make sense of the world, navigate competing priorities, set and pursue goals, etc.

It’s how we do every day.

If the very nature of who you are and how you view yourself is threatened, it gets really scary.

Without that, what do you have? Who are you without … yourself?

As long as we hold that fear, we’ll never be fully alive. We’re beholden to the narrative and story. Anything that could violate that story is a threat.

​

The Stoics talk about the Moment Mori — remembering you will die. It’s a concept that transcends traditions.

Early Buddhist texts use the word “maraṇasati,” meaning remember death.

In fact, Theravada Buddhists have a death meditation. They look on decaying corpses and say, “that is me.“

The work is to embrace the truth of a future death so that you can be fully alive.

There’s a parallel here to whatever you’re trying to do, create, and make: you have a fear of some kind of death. Not a physical death. But an ego death.

I had a big one. And I didn’t know it until it happened.

For the past 10+ years I’ve been an entrepreneur. I spent my days building business and freelancing. It’s a longer story for another time. But over the past few months I’ve had to face the reality that I might need a more steady income and take a W2.

Suddenly the possibility of the Death of Dan the Entrepreneur loomed in my future.

I had to face the reality that maybe I won’t be an entrepreneur.

Maybe not in the next season of work, and maybe never again. I wrestled with this. I shed tears over it. I fought it.

And then I accepted it. And I began to feel free.

​

What I found on the other side was the beautiful truth that I so often forget:

Something as small as this can’t define me.

I found that you can take the boy out of entrepreneurship, but you can’t take the entrepreneur out of the boy.

I found once again the truth that who I am and what I have to give is so much bigger than any single role or even a single path.

When I came to see it this way, the world opened up. I had options.
I can do what I want and what feels right for me and my family without holding to a singular fragile self-narrative.

Only when we free ourselves from the fear of death can we be fully alive. If we want to be free, we have to face death.

What do I mean by free? I mean that holding tight to a single story costs a lot!

If I’m terrified of loosing my entrepreneurship story, what could it cost me?

Opportunities. Income. A better future for my family. How I spend my time. What I work on. How much stress I carry.

Imagine it. And then imagine facing the very thing you’re running from. Imagine living out that worst case scenario. And imagine being ok with it.

​

The irony of all of this is that...

The fear of losing parts of ourselves keeps us from the things we want most.

In other words: your fear is bigger than your desire.

Here’s an example: Let’s say you want to be a brilliant writer. Great.

To do that you have to write the book, edit the book, publish the book, and promote the book. Now what if the brilliance of your author self depended on the success of each of those steps?

First you have to write brilliant words. Then you have to have an editor make them even more brilliant. Then you have to share those brilliant words with people who may or may not think they’re brilliant. Then you have to promote it over and over again, hoping that the brilliance comes through.

Good lord that’s a lot of pressure!

You’re beholden to that narrative in a way that makes your path forward very fragile. You’re not free. You’re not living your best life. You’re scared and your actions are limited.

And that fear is going to cause you to play it safe. And when you play it safe, the things you create aren’t brilliant.

This is to say: embrace the death of your dreams. Lean into and meditate on the loss of what you most hold dear. And in so doing, may you find freedom.

One more story: I’ve been putting off sending this email for month. I’ve been afraid of starting the newsletter back up. Afraid of people unsubscribing. Afraid that I don’t have anything valuable to say. Afraid that I’m irrelevant. Afraid that what I’ve been trying to build for the past 10+ years with The Meaning Movement doesn’t have much momentum.

I let that story keep me locked up.

And so, I spent time on the death of the Meaning Movement. What would it feel like if everyone unsubscribed? What would it feel like if no one read and listened? What if my site traffic went away? What if my online friends stopped responding? What if everything was deleted?

It would hurt. I would feel sad. And then I would feel free.

So this email, in itself, is my death mediation.

I hope you’ll find yours.

Here's to finding the freedom you need to live your most courageous and free life.

Yours in meaning making,

PS- I'm working on rebooting the podcast and hope to have semi-regular newsletters landing in your inbox.

In the meantime, hit reply. I'd love to hear what you're excited about making/creating/doing in this season of life. I can't promise to respond, but I promise I read every email.

PPS - I'm sharing abbreviated versions of ideas like this on LinkedIn regularly. Would love to have you follow along there: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dancumberland/

Dan Cumberland

Say hi 👋 on Twitter or LinkedIn!

And follow along:

​​​​

What's your Super Power?

🖤 Want people to follow you into battle? I found the secret...
​
Last week a friend asked me what my super power is.
​
(Great question, right? I want your answer in the comments!)
​
My answer was this:
​
😭 I cry a lot.
​
That's not actually the super power, but it points to the power.
​
🤩 The power is heart centered and empathic connection.
​
I've never been a part of a community that wasn't described as special by the people who are a part of it. For a long time I couldn't figure out what makes that kind of magic.
​
I eventually connected the dots back to the fact that I feel a lot. Sometimes too much.
​
But people respond to feeling. People want to be heard. Seen. Felt.
​
So if you're trying to move people, let them see your vulnerability.
​
If you want to be a better leader, feel something for the people you lead.
​
Be open. Be weak. Be human.
​
In a world dominated by heartless businesses, there are a lot of us who crave a different narrative and experience.

If you dare enough to show up, you might be surprised to see what happens next. 🖤

💡An Idea

Brute Force isn't the Answer

🎃 I used to hate carving pumpkins. Until I realized something...
​
I was afraid I'd cut myself. They knives weren't agile enough. It was annoying.
​
But my kids loved it.
​
Every year I'd dread the day I had to manage the pumpkins. Until one day I stopped and thought: how else can I do this? What would make this easy?
​
And then I realized I own a jig saw. What was I doing?!?
​
The thing is, I had been doing it the old and inefficient way for years while the jig saw sat in a box in the shed.
​
That's so often how things go as entrepreneurs and leaders. We do things the way they've always been done because they work, and we don't always have the bandwidth to change things.
​
The problem is those brute force efforts stack up. If you don't take a moment to recalibrate and get clear on where you're trying to go and why — you're going to burn out, blow things up, or otherwise some very expensive mistakes (I'm sure ER rooms see plenty of pumpkin carving knife wounds...)

You Can't Create Change

🤐 You can’t change people, but you can do this instead…
​
So much of the results of our leadership come down to other people. I don’t like that. Don’t get me wrong: I like people. But I don’t like how little control I have over the choices that other people make.

I’ve been participating in the amazing work that Seth Godin and a massive team of volunteers are doing to help empower individuals to fight climate change with the Carbon Almanac (check it out if you haven’t: TheCarbonAlmanac.org )
​
One thing that Seth reiterates to us repeatedly is that we’re “creating the condition for change”.
​
We lead with our action. Our actions create an environment in which other people choose to act.
​
🔑 There’s a difference.
​
You can’t make people change. But you can create the conditions in which the choice to change is easier.
​
⛏ Do your work.
🙌 Make your contribution.
​
And then let others make their choices.
​
Let's go! 🚀

"My barn having burned to the ground,

The end, with it's pain and loss, unlocks new places inside you.

content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan Cumberland. My focus is work, meaning, and personal development. I’m here to help you level up your life, career, and income. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Happy thanksgiving week for those who are celebrating. It has been a wild ride in my life in the last few days. I have some really fun updates in the works. It's enough to make your head spin!

But each of those topics will have to wait for their moment in the spotlight.

As for right now, the biggest news is that we just wrapped up Season 10 of the podcast! It's a milestone for me and the team. Thanks for your continued support. More on that below. So let's get to it...

Here's what we have for you today:

💌 An invite

💡 An Idea

🎙 On the Podcast

❤️ Fun Things I'm Enjoying

Let's do this! 🚀

💌 An invite

RISE Summit

I had the great opportunity to be a part of the RISE Summit, alongside a bunch of other great thought leaders in the personal development space.

I'd love for you to check out the summit here: https://risesummits.com/DanCumberland​

You'll get to learn myself and other great thinkers with ideas around Mission, Vision, and Impact.

In my sessions I share some thoughts on how changing how you view your past reframes the way you live in the present. The session is titled: How to Find Freedom from Your Past, Live Fully in the Present, and Create a Brighter Future

The summit is free to watch and starts in a couple of days.

Click here to Join

💡 An Idea

You Don't Need a Why

❌ You don’t need a why...
​
We hear all the time how important it is to have a clear “why” in your life and business.
​
🧐 But have you ever thought about WHY you need a why?
​
Yes, I know the answer:
✔️ So you’ll be able to recall it when things are hard
✔️ So you can make sure all the decisions you’re making are taking you to in the right direction.
✔️ Etc.
​
Those are all fine. And I drank that kool-aid for a long time on all of that.
​
But here’s the problem:
IF what you’re doing is so personally challenging and painful that you have to remind yourself WHY you’re doing it, then you have a problem.
​
Most entrepreneurs don’t have a WHY problem. We have a HOW problem.
​
❌ If your pace is unsustainable, clarifying your why won’t help.
​
❌ If you’re over-working yourself, knowing WHY isn’t going keep you healthy.
​
❌ If you’re making less money than you need to be, spending more time than you want to be, and experiencing more stress than you should be — your why isn’t going to help.
​
Change your “how”.
​
✅ How you live your days is how you live your life.
​
I’ve burned out hard on this path, and I know from experience that when how you’re building your business and pursuing your goals is fun and balanced, the why takes care of itself.
​
Stop sacrificing yourself to a life you don't love in order to gain a future that may never come.
​
If you're with me, tell me in the comments. I want to know that I'm not the only one.
​
And if you need help course correcting your entrepreneurial path, I'm here for you.
​

Read and Comment on LinkedIn

Developing the Owner’s Mindset with Alex Sanfilippo

My guest today is Alex Sanfilippo. He owns a company dedicated to helping podcasters. I love and use many of the products that he is creating.

I met Alex some time ago when I was a guest on his podcast, and since then, I've continued to watch him create more and more resources to serve this target demographic. And it has been so much fun.

It was great to have him on the show. What I loved about this conversation is we got to get into the mindset of an entrepreneur and how he developed that mindset even before he was an entrepreneur. We talked about the difference between an intrapreneur and an entrepreneur. You could think of it as having an entrepreneur mindset and taking that mindset to your work— even if you're working for someone else.

It was just a fantastic conversation. You'll just hear Alex's passion come through. He's just an incredible guy doing some incredible things.

🎙 On the Podcast

💡 An Idea:

Surrendering the Dream

I've been thinking how much we idealize what could be in life. This applies to so much: careers, relationships, creative pursuits, parenting, etc.

No matter how hard we try though, what we get in life is never the ideal. This can be both disappointing and liberating.

There's much to be gained by holding on to our dreams loosely and chasing after them, while also letting go of the specifics.

We must make room for the details to be different from the dream.

It can be helpful to feel disappointed by this gap. It's only by feeling the disappointment that you're able to accept your current reality for what it is.

Maybe you don't have the perfect job, spouse, child, life, etc. But what you have may be very good.

In fact, what you have may even be better than what you wanted — if you have the eyes to see it.

I hope you'll have the courage to do so.

subject: FAQ's for The Calling Course
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan Cumberland. My focus is work, meaning, and personal development. I’m here to help you level up your life, career, and income. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

As you know may know, we've opened up enrollment for The Calling Course for a limited time.

If you didn’t, I’d like to invite you to watch the free training I did on How to Avoid, Survive, and Thrive in a Career Crisis (it’s one of the most important pieces I’ve created in a while): https://youtu.be/2VPRcxoXa_Q​

Then check out the Calling Course here: http://thecallingcourse.com/new​

Both are only available for the next week so watch, read, and dig in ASAP.

I want to make sure you are well-informed about the course for the following reasons:

Reason #1: The results of taking the course and putting it into action are going to be HUGE for most of you.

Reason #2: I care about you and your process. Really, this work is so important to me and I’m so grateful to have you as a part of it. So much so, that I’m giving away 12 months of unlimited coaching with me for everyone who joins during this launch.

Reason #3: Enrollment is closing in a few days

Reason #4: Even IF the course isn’t a fit for you, I hope you pick up some learning lessons from the Career Crisis training and emails I’ve sent along the way.

I've received some GREAT questions about the Calling Course that I wanted to answer.

If you haven't checked out the course, you can do so here: http://thecallingcourse.com/new​

Otherwise, i'm going to dig into some of these questions for the rest of this email.

Question #1: Is this course right for me? Meaning, will it “work” for me?

Everyone is in different places and carrying degrees of buy-in, so I can’t guarantee that your results will be the same— there are just so many variables. But what I can say is this: I’m giving you the exact blueprint that has helped thousands of others. And I hold your hand step-by-step through the process. I don’t leave anything for you to have to figure it out on your own.

AND I’ve never had anyone give it their all and not benefit from it. This process is just too deep. You can’t go to the places that we go and not come out the other side without some major (dare I say life changing?) results.

The system works. If you put in the effort, this course will help you tremendously.

Question #2: What exactly do I get with the course?

Great question. This is all laid out on the course’s registration page, but here are the juicy details in case that’s easier:

⚡️ After completing registration and payment you get immediate access to all 8 modules of the course in a beautifully deigned member's area.

⚡️ You get 24/7 access. This includes any and all future updates to the course.

⚡️ The course material is video based teaching (featuring yours truly!).

And if that wasn’t enough, you get these killer bonuses:

✅ The Purpose Planner Workbook that takes you through each of the lessons and homework in a step-by-step manner. Simply download it and print, or keep it digital. It’s up to you!

✅ The Calling Resource Cheat Sheet— a download cheatsheet of all my favorite resources for finding and doing work that matters. IF you want to dig deeper into any of the concepts from the course, the cheatsheet will have you covered!

✅ Email swipe copy— you have the opportunity to bring others into your process in a really incredible way. This swipe copy gives you a copy and paste, word-for-word method for reaching out.

✅ Members only Facebook group — a great place to connect with and learn from other people in the course and community.

✅ MONTHLY Ask Me Anything Sessions — we're hoping on live to answer all your questions about the course, your process, and anything else that you might be curious about.

Plus, for this launch I’m opening up a few CRAZY bonuses that I’ve never offered before (and who knows: I may never offer again! It depends how much you make me work for it! haha).

Exclusive Bonuses (this launch only):

✨ Unlimited Coaching - I’m going to give everyone who joins my direct booking link for the next 12 months. I’ll personally jump on with you and help in any way that I can.

✨ Unlimited Direct Email Support - If you’re less of a live coaching kind of person and prefer a more passive engagement, I’ve got you covered. You get direct email support from me for your first 12 months. Just email me with any questions you have and I’ll get back to you ASAP.

✨ Unlimited Guarantee with no time bounds - I want to take all the risk out of your experience joining, so I’m giving you an unlimited guarantee. As long as you actually do the work, if you don’t get any benefit from the course, I’ll give you a full refund.

Question #3: How long are the modules?

Each module is on average around 30-minutes, plus bonus videos, and some highly effective exercises. The point isn’t how long the content is, but how effective it is in helping you make progress.

Question #4: How long do I get access for?

You get access for the lifetime of the course. Plus you get unlimited updates. The course is always 100% up to date and if anything ever changes I'm in there to update it...I'll never leave you hanging.

Question #5: How long on average will it take for me to get results?

It depends on how hard you work. The average is around 90 days. But it can be done much quicker if you’re ready to get your hands dirty!

The good news is that once you do it, it continues to offer benefits for years to come. Many people end up coming back and reviewing the material over the years to recalibrate and remind themselves in times of transition.

The quicker you dig in, the quicker the results.

Question #6: If I do a payment plan do I get the full course or just some part of it?

You get full access. The payment plan is just there to make it easier for you to jump in. There’s no penalty or restrictions. It’s all the same material, 100%.

There are two payment options:

Option #1: full payment of $597

Option #2: 5 Payments of $127. $127 due at check out and then once a month for the next 4 months (for a total of 5 payments, including checkout).

Some people in the business world think it’s crazy to give full access to people who aren’t paid in full. But I love getting you going as fast as you want to go. Plus, I’m generally a really trusting person. I don’t think you’re out there to screw me out of my material and work. If you are, please don’t 😉

Question #7: You said the course is step-by-step. Is it really step-by-step?

Yes! It takes you through the process and leaves nothing out. Every module leads to the next with specific exercises in-between.

It like having someone with you saying, “do this, then this, then this.” All the way through.

There’s so much confusion and ambiguity in the realm of calling and purpose. These are complicated and deep topics! But I wanted to clear it up for all of us and make this as straight forward as possible.

Question #8: Is this course faith based? Do I need to have a specific worldview or faith orientation?

No. The course is not faith based. You do not need to hold a specific system for it to work. In fact, I’ve had everyone from Christians, Atheists, and all kinds of other belief systems go through this material and benefit from it. The word “calling” is tricky like that, as it does often bring up religious connotations. But this course, like all of my material, is not religious in nature.

Question #9: This sounds great. How do I sign up?

I’m so glad you asked! Actually, I planted this question 😆

Everything is right here: http://thecallingcourse.com/new​

Question #10: WAIT! I have more questions!

No problem! Hit reply and I’ll respond!

If you haven’t checked it out yet, go here are the juicy details: http://thecallingcourse.com/new​

I’ll see you there!

-Dan

subject: Transformational moments [+ workshop replay]
content:
Hi Friends,

A few days ago I hosted a new workshop called How to Avoid a Career Crisis. If you were one of the folks who joined live, THANK YOU! I had a blast! I’m still feeling so energized by the experience!

If you weren’t able to join, no worries! Here is the replay link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2VPRcxoXa_Q​

As I shared in the training, career and life crisis are incredibly human and normal experience — even though they usually don’t feel like it.

We don’t talk about them enough when we’re in them.

It makes sense though. We all feel this pressure to have it all together and have it all figured out. And the essence of these transitional moments in life is that you don’t have it figured out.

But I’m here to say: that’s ok! It’s great in fact!

How can I say that? Because the moment you let yourself not have it all figured out is the moment you open yourself up to receive what is emerging in your life and become who you are being called to be.

I use that word, “called” loosely — because it can have a lot of baggage. I’m not talking about some mystical permanent ball and chain calling that you must bear. Instead, I’m talking about you becoming more fully who you are. You letting your identity guide you and living into the best possible version of yourself in the world.

This is why I get so fired up about career and life crises! They’re such powerful moments in our lives that are just teeming with latent potential. They’re an opportunity to grab ahold of your life, take it by the horns, and make it into a life you love passionately.

How amazing would that be?

Or, let me reframe that for us: how amazing WILL that be?

THIS is the stuff that gets me fired up. And this is why I was so excited to share this training with you.

This could change your life. I know it has changed mine.

I hope you’ll take some time to watch the training.

To your success,

-Dan

PS- Whether or not the Calling Course is right for you, I hope you'll watch this training. I believe it's some of the most important content that I've created recently: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2VPRcxoXa_Q​

Hi Friends,

I'm holding a free live training at Noon PST today. I hope you'll join. Here's why:

Work is a journey of identity.

At its best, it's an invitation to make something that matters to us in the world.

At it's worst, it's a soul sucking prison.

But the truth is that much of work happens between those extremes.

And in tandem with our day-in-and-day-out work life is happening. We're having families, pursuing goals. We're celebrating the highs, grieving the lows, and everything in between.
