subject: A confession...
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan Cumberland. My focus is work, meaning, career, and personal development. I’m here to help you level up your life, career, and income. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "there" }},

A big welcome to the new folks who joined the email list this week! I'm thrilled that you're here.

In this week's issue we have: a big (and this time very personal) idea (*gulp*), a podcast, and a roundup of a few fun things (as usual).

Let's get into it!

Double or Nothing: a Confession

*Deep breath... This next part is tough.*

When you get close to your work in the world — not your job, but the work you were made to do — there are a lot of ways that fear and self-sabotage can interfere.

I've been building the Meaning Movement online for 8 years. In that time, I've only spent a few years really focused on it.

Why? Oh, I can give you a million reasons to justify it. But the real reason is that I've been hiding.

I'm so afraid of going ALL IN on something that I care this much about.

I'm so afraid of putting too much of my heart and soul into something and have it land flat.

And there are stories behind this. I could tell you about failed attempts at launches and growth and how much they haunt me.

But I'll save those stories for another time.

The point is this (and I hate even writing it, but it's truth and needs to be said): I've been hiding from this work, trying to protect myself from past pain, and keeping it at arm's distance.

I believe, more than anything in the world, that you have something to say. You have a gift to give. And I want desperately to be a part of helping you find it, create it, and live into it.

It's a meta, but I know that is my work: helping you find and do yours.

AND YET, it's so much easier for me to keep busy, be "reasonable", play it safe, and keep myself distracted.

Over the past few months I've been realizing this. And I'm beginning the process of leaning in and facing those fears.

But there comes a time when you have to leap. For me, this is that moment. I'm going double or nothing. I'm investing myself, my energy, and any resources that I can muster into taking the Meaning Movement to a new place.

I'm terrified. But also excited.

And I can't do it alone.

Which is where you come in.

If you want to be a part of this journey with me, there are a few easy ways that I'd love to have your help. Reply to this email and I'll follow up with you there. Just say, "I'm in." And I'll respond back.

Thanks for reading. Thanks being a part of this.

With so much gratitude 🙏 🙏 🙏

The Podcast

Vanessa Van Edwards is a recovering awkward person and introvert who is on a mission to help everyone learn how to engage, interact, and lead with authenticity and genuine engagement. What that means is that she's teaching people how to interpret and use the many verbal and non-verbal cues that often go unnoticed so you can feel more at ease and in control of how you show up.

It's really fun stuff. I'm very into it. I've learned a lot from her that I'm already putting into practice.

Vanessa is the Lead Investigator at Science of People. She is the bestselling author of Captivate: The Science of Succeeding with People. More than 50 million people have watched her YouTube tutorials and TEDx Talk.

She works with entrepreneurs, growing businesses, and trillion-dollar companies; and has been featured all over the web.

More than anything, what I love about Vanessa is how she practices what she preaches. She's warm, engaging, and a fantastic communicator.

🎧 Listen in or read along here: themeaningmovement.com/vanessa 🎧

Things I'm Enjoying

🥳 Throwing better parties! My friend and recent podcast guest, Nick Gray just released a book about throwing parties and it's on sale for $1.99 on kindle right now. It's practical, fun, and can be applied to just about any type of party you'd like to host. My wife and I have been using his method to throw cocktail parties. I used some of his technics at my birthday party. It's fantastic. I'd love for you to pick up a copy: https://amzn.to/3O179Np .

In fact, if you're in the pacific northwest and want to come to one of our parties, hit reply and let me know!

📚 A few fun books I'm reading:

As mentioned above, I'm doubling down on the Meaning Movement and as such, I'm having to face some fears, anxieties, trauma, and limiting beliefs. As I do, I've been reading some great books about mindset. While these might be a bit out there for some, they're hitting me right where I need it right now:

  • 📕 Breaking the Habit of Being Yourself: How to Lose Your Mind and Create a New One by Joe Dispenza - This book is part pop-psychology, part quantum physics, and part mindset. It's great and is helping me see how much I (still) limit my future by my beliefs about what's possible.
    ​
  • 📘 You Are a Badass at Making Money: Master the Mindset of Wealth by Jen Sincero - Much like the book above, this one helps you unpack all your thoughts, feelings, and fears about money, making money, and your self worth. Again, it's exactly what I need right now.
    ​
  • What are you reading? Anything you'd recommend?

Yours in meaning making,

-Dan

PS- Have you enjoyed content from me and The Meaning Movement? You can support our content creation via a monthly gift of $5, $10, or $25. Or you can share this newsletter with a friend.

subject: Building a Network, Hosting Cocktail Parties, and the Importance of Hobby Projects with Nick Gray
content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan Cumberland. My focus is work, meaning, and personal development. I’m here to help you level up your life, career, and income. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "there" }},

Holy moly it's been a week!

My family has been battling a big bout of stomach flu for the past few days. Thankfully my wife and I seem to have dodged the bullet (*knock on wood*), but my poor kids certainly didn't. 🤢

I have three kids 6 and under and they were troopers through the whole thing.

We had a literal scoreboard to track how many... well... maybe this is TMI. But you get the picture.

We made the most of it. They're healthy and heading back to school in the next few days to round out their school years.

I was planning on showing up in your inbox last week — not that you're keeping track. But I've been... indisposed.

I hope this finds you and yours healthier than me and mine have been.

Now onto this week's content!

This week we have:

🙋‍♂️ a question that I REALLY want you to respond to (please!)
🔉 a new and very personal podcast episode
📝 and a round up of some favorite things.

Question: What Best Describes Your Interest in Meaning?

The Meaning Movement has a wide audience. As I seek to serve you better, I'd like to know more about you and your interest in the topics that I create around. Below is a list of identifiers, could you hit reply and let me know which resonate the most (if any) and what else you'd add?

"I'm MOST interested in ____________"

  • Finding meaning in my career
  • Finding meaning outside of my career
  • Finding meaning post-work/in-retirement
  • Starting/growing a project that I'm passionate about
  • Making a career change
  • Increasing my income
  • Personal development (productivity, mindset, creativity, etc.)

Please hit reply and let me know! THANK YOU in advance.

On The Podcast

Nick Gray has scaled and sold multiple businesses. He's the founder of Museum Hack, which started as a fun way to engage with art and artifacts and then grew much bigger than he ever imagined. He was also an important part of growing and selling a business his father started.
​
Today he does a lot of things. He's always sharing his adventures and experiences online and in his newsletter, which I personally really enjoy reading and following. Most relevant to my life and our conversation, he's been developing a method for hosting parties that I've been using. And it's been a blast.
​
We'll get into all of that in the interview, so I don't want to spoil it here.
​
But what I do want to say is that I really like Nick. He's approachable and open. He has a comfortable and genuine air about him, that I really appreciate. He's the kind of person who makes you feel at ease. And I've really enjoyed getting to know him in this conversation and beyond.

🎧 Listen in or read along here: themeaningmovement.com/nick-gray 🎧

Things I'm Enjoying

☕️ Fellow Shimmy Coffee Sieve - I love good coffee and roast my own at home (I know! geek alert!) and coffee items often end up in this section of the newsletter. This one was a surprise. I didn't even know it existed until my wife bought it for my as a birthday present. It's a simple and elegant tool that allows you sift out the "fines" from your coffee, after it is ground and before you brew. I'd been experimenting with sifting via a tea strainer — and this is way more fun. The result is a much more clean tasting cup of coffee. The difference is very noticeable and I honestly can't believe it's taken me this long to discover this!

🍹 Cocktail Parties! - We've been hosting cocktail parties every month or so this year as a way to build connections with and among our community. It talk about this at length in the podcast with Nick above, as he's been a huge inspiration for us to do this. As I told Nick recently, 2022 has been a rough year in many ways — both personally and professionally. There's been a lot of hard stuff happening. And yet our cocktail parties have been a consistent bright spot. Listen to the episode if you haven't. You might enjoy doing something similar!

📕 We Should All Be Millionaires by Rachel Rodgers - I'm not the target demographic for this book. It's written for women and especially with women of color in mind. I'm male and white. But all the more reason to me that I should read it. Rodgers is inspiring in her approach to business and in her reframing of the narratives that we (and women in particular) have around work, money, and life. It was great. I'll probably read it again.

Yours in meaning making,

-Dan

content:
👋 Hi! I'm Dan Cumberland. My focus is work, meaning, career, and personal development. I’m here to help you level up your life, career, and income. If that sounds good, let's go! 🚀

Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "there" }},

My family just arrived in San Francisco where we'll be living for the next few weeks. It's not a "vacation", as I'm still working as usual. But it's fun to experience a new place and explore a new city.

So far I'm very impressed by both the density of the city (it feels very different from my "city life" in Seattle), and the hills! I knew they had hills here, I'm blow away by how much my running pace has dropped 😆

Today we have a Workshop Replay, a request, a podcast, and a roundup of a few fun things (as usual). Let's get into it!

You Should Be EXCITED for Your Next Career Crisis (🎥 Workshop Replay)

Last week I had a BLAST hosted a new workshop called How to Avoid a Career Crisis. If you were one of the folks who joined live, THANK YOU! I had a blast! I’m still feeling so energized by the experience!

If you weren’t able to join, no worries! Here is the replay link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2VPRcxoXa_Q​

As I shared in the training, career and life crisis are incredibly human and normal experience — even though they usually don’t feel like it.

We don’t talk about them enough when we’re in them.

It makes sense though. We all feel this pressure to have it all together and have it all figured out. And the essence of these transitional moments in life is that you don’t have it figured out.

But I’m here to say: that’s ok! It’s great in fact!

You should watch the replay to find out why 😃

Watch here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2VPRcxoXa_Q​

At the end, I share about the Calling Course and offer an epic bonus for the first few folks that join. If you join in the next week, I'll extend that to you as well. So chickity-check-it-out!

What do you want to learn next?

I'm doing at least one live training every month (see above). I'd love to know what you'd like to learn. Hit reply and let me know! I'd love your help shaping the content!

The Podcast

Corey Frey is a multi-disciplinary artist, poet, art educator, husband and father of two children. He and his wife currently live in Frederick, Maryland where he works at a local non-profit Art Center and leads The Well Collaborative — a community dedicated to recognizing the creative potential in the people they share their lives with.

In his artwork, Corey finds inspiration in nature and the interconnectedness of all things. He enjoys playing with language, color, shadow, light and much more.

In this interview we talk about Corey’s life as a creative and artist, his relationship with art, and how he supports and builds community with and for fellow artists.

🎧 Listen in or read along here: themeaningmovement.com/corey 🎧

Things I'm Enjoying

🌁 San Francisco! It's fun here! And who knew there's an emoji of the Golden Gate Bridge with 🌁 and without 🌉 fog! 😆

💡 Idea: get out of your own way. I'm continually working to identify how much I get in my own way and make life harder for myself. For example: I needed to record a bunch of videos for the next season of the podcast. We're bringing the show to YouTube and 4x'ing our production. I want to look and sound good, so it's tempting to spend a lot of time getting the lighting and the camera just right. And then I need to get ready. Maybe I should take a shower and shave? Maybe I should change my shirt between takes? Maybe I should brush my teeth?
​
OR maybe I just need to call it good enough and get it done.

Which is what I ended up doing then.

(And here I'm doing it again with this email 😅)

Sure. It'd be nice to have it be perfect. But it's better to have it done.

Pay attention to how much you might be complicating things in life. You'll be surprised.

Yours in meaning making,

-Dan

subject: Finding Your True Voice
content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

How do you think about calling and vocation? When you think about those ideas in your life today, what form do they take?

When I interview creatives about their work, I often ask them how they think about the idea of voice and how they found their voices in their art and creativity.

But talking to artists about it is simply a shortcut.

It’s easy to talk to them about it because the arts have space for related ideas. If you’re an artist you recognize that you have a style. You must.

If you’re creating something that other interact with, you have to be intentional about your artistic perspective. Sometime you even need to write artist statements, where you have to articulate bits of all of this.

The challenge for the rest of us non-artists is that we still have a voice, yet our chosen fields give us less opportunities to think intentionally about it. Instead, it’s a concept that stirs something in us, yet leaves us uncertain how to engage with it.

I’d like to tackle this head on.

Everyone has a voice. YES! Even you! Not only that but your voice has everything to do with who you were made to be, what you were made to do, and how you find meaning, purpose, and fulfillment in your work.

Your voice is the narrative arch that holds your life and work story together.

I dive deep into this idea in the Calling Course, which is open for enrollment at our lowest ever available price for the next few days. Join here: thecallingcourse.com/new​

Whether or not you decide to join the course, I want to invite you to think about your work and your voice as an important part of what you bring to the world.

No matter your job and no matter your chosen career, your work is its best when you show up in it, with your voice and your full presence.

Sure. Not every workplace and work expression is going to accommodate this whole heatedly— but we all know when we’ve seen it and felt it.

There's a woman who works at the post office I typically go to who brings so much life to the room. She knows her customers by name. She's makes them smile. She laughs. She creates something meaningful in a job that is known for being dry and even soul-sucking.

She uses her voice. And it changes the world around her. You can't be around her and not notice.

When we strip it all back, you find that your voice is you. And your calling in the world is to bring about the truest and most authentic version of that in whatever context you’re able to.

This is what my work is about. And I hope every day that I’m able to help you do this in your life.

If you’d like to engage with me more intentionally around these ideas, please take a moment to consider the Calling Course. It takes you step-by-step through my process of finding, naming, and living into your true voice and work in the world.

It’s open for enrollment for a few more days, and I’d be honored to have you join us.

I lowered the price for the lowest it's ever been. I'd like to invite you to take a step deeper into who you are in the world, to find more meaning and purpose, and to find and use your voice more fully.

See everything I have waiting for you here: thecallingcourse.com/new​

To you and your future,

-Dan

That’s how these things go. They just creep up on you and then you look up and realize that something’s not right.

It’s not a huge surprise. It’s been a heavy season personally. I’ve mentioned this before. My grandmother passed away. I lost a core business partner. I’ve been dealing with some big things.

It creeps up on you without you even knowing it, and then you’re in it. Call it being stuck. Call it a fog. It’s as though you’ve taken your eyes off the map, made a wrong turn, and have no idea where you are.

It’s in this space that I’ve returned to the Calling Course material personally as a way to help clear my head. I developed The Meaning Method (which the course is based on) from my research in grad school, my own personal experience, and my one-on-one client work.

Below we have a new episode of the podcast and some of the things in life that I'm into right now. Read on and enjoy!

On the Podcast

Super Smack is on a rapping, dancing, music-making journey to uplift and inspire anyone who has ever felt underrepresented. He writes thoughtful lyrics that reflect on his experiences and refers to his music as underdog pop.
​
His career path has spanned everything from cyber security and project management to Broadway and recording and releasing hip hop albums.
​
Inspired by an eclectic combination of K-Pop, Outkast and Lin-Manuel Miranda, Smack has created a unique sound style that he calls “A-Pop”: Asian, American, Arizonan. After releasing his debut EP “Neon Red" at SXSW in 2019, he went on to co-headline the CRAZY SWITCH ASIANS tour, performing in 16 cities in three weeks.
​
In 2021 he released his follow up EP “Neon Blue” while also collaborating with fellow Phoenix rapper Mega Ran on the single “Black X Gold”, which was selected for Rolling Stone's Global Artist Spotlight.
​
After living the past 10 years in New York City, Super Smack recently moved back to his original home city of Phoenix, Arizona. With his roots set in a new home, he has begun recording his debut full-length album, which releases later this year.

🎧 Listen in or read along here: themeaningmovement.com/smack 🎧

  • What Super Smack does

subject: What is a Sextant anyway?
content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

My work, at its best, is to help you find and do your best work in the world.

I don’t take that lightly. It’s a big responsibility.

And over the years I’ve tried to create as many ways as possible for you to engage with me on this. From the blog, podcast, books, and also, The Calling Course. It’s all here to help you.

No matter how you hear from me, there’s one thing I’m trying to do: help you find your way.

You could think of me as your guide (in fact I have a toy Yoda on my desk to help remind me of that role!).

And in everything that I do I’m trying to help you find your way.

I want to invite you to think for a moment about what that would feel like. What would your body tell you if you knew your direction, what you wanted to offer the world, and how you wanted to offer it?

This is what I created the Calling Course to do. It helps you make your map. It serves as a GPS. It’s the compass or sextant that is always there to guide you.

I wish I could say that it’s clean, simple, easy, and painless — it can be — but it often is not. But the process is important and good.

If we’re honest, we all know that that easy usually disappoints and that the most beautiful parts of life come with the price tag of some work to earn them.

This is true of what I’m inviting you to with the Calling Course.

I’ve opened the doors for a limited time and I’d like to invite you to join us.

Click here to see everything that is waiting for you: https://thecallingcourse.com/flash​

It’s a self paced course that takes you deep into your own work and world to answer the big questions of life: who are you, where are you going, what do you want to give, and where do you want to give it?

Along the way you have access to me via email and monthly via live Q&A’s. In fact, I’m committed to helping you via the live calls no matter how long it takes you to get through the material. It’s a resource you can always come back to.

So if you’d like to have a better understanding of what you were put on this earth to do — I can’t give you the answer, but I can lead you through a process that will help that answer become clear.

Click here to join the course. I can’t wait to support you on your journey.

content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "there" }},

I've been traveling over the last couple of weeks to attend to some family things. As I transition into life back home, I'm reminded of how nice familiar spaces and routines are. I'm able to feel more on top of my tasks and responsibilities when I'm in a rhythm — and my home and workspace help facilitate that in ways that I take for granted.

Below is content on the podcast this week, as well some of my favorite things of the past few weeks.

Read on and let me know how you're doing!

On the Podcast

Ronsley Vaz is a man of many talents. His work has been diverse — from being a software engineer to financial advisor to a chef. Now he primarily helps entrepreneurs by guiding them to use their voice, something we care a lot about around here.

As you'll hear in this interview, his journey with finding and embracing his voice goes back to his childhood, which is true for many of us as we search for and find our voices. With his work today he helps business owners find what matters, speak their inner truths, and solve meaningful problems in the world.

  • Understanding and managing social media content outreach
  • Own your identity and be authentic

Things I'm Enjoying

😴 Taking a break - I push myself hard when it comes to fitness. I'm training to break my personal record and complete a 5k in 18 minutes. I'm also very disciplined with calisthenics. But I've been experiencing new pains and tightness recently that is causing me to slow down a bit. I don't always like it, but I'm working on giving myself permission to just take a break and have a few days off. Rest is good, especially when you've worked hard beforehand.

📚 The Almanack of Navel Ravikant - I've been listening to this over the past week while running and on the plane. Navel is an interesting person to me, as he resides at the intersection of entrepreneurship/Venture Capital and Philosophy — a pretty unique space. There are many interesting insights that it has left me pondering. Here's two of them paraphrased:

  • If you're having a hard time deciding between directions to go, choose the one that is more difficult up front. You're likely resisting the short term pain while that path will lead to longer term gains.
    ​
  • Throughout the book Navel mentions that he wants to live in such a way that takes luck out of the equation. As he puts it, if there are 1,000 versions of reality, he is successful in 999 of them.

It's been a fun read/listen.

🎠 Disneyland. I have three kids 6 and under. My wife and I took them to Disneyland for the first time last week. It was a really fun and happy counterpoint to some of the loss and grief we've been feeling.

My favorite moment was seeing my three year old waving with all her might at her favorite characters and just lighting up when they waved back. It was really special.

🐥 Twitter. You can learn so much from twitter. Follow people who are doing what you want to do more of and learn from them. It's a great resource. Here's where you can find me. Come say hi!

How about you? What have you been enjoying? Hit reply and let me know.

subject: An invitation to face your fears
content:
{% if subscriber.first_name != blank %}
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name }},
{% else %}
Hi Meanies,
{% endif %}

I've been studying transitions and transformation for a long time, since the early 2000's. And there's on particular aspect that all transitions have in common: fear.

Fear of the unknown.

Fear of being known.

Fear of loss.

Fear of what people might think.

Fear of relationships changing.

Fear of actually succeeding.

So. Much. To. fear!

But I've also learned a few things about fear: the more you face it, and spend time with it, the more you're able to create the kind of change that you dream about making.

Which is why I created Fearless February. Fearless February is free movement to help you take calculated risk toward your goals in the month of February. I even built a simple site for it years ago: fearlessfebruary.com.

In past years we've made a whole thing of it: a facebook group, emails, live calls, etc.

This year I'm taking a different approach. It's just an open invitation to do something that matters to you that fear may be holding you back on. Maybe February could be the month you gently and courageously step into it.

Maybe you'll find your brave pants (I think you will).

Maybe you'll find your fear is louder than the actual risk (it usually is).

Maybe it will change you (I know it can).

If you need a formal invitation to do so, this is it and if you've been waiting for permission, here it is.

All I ask is that you do something.

And if you'd like to tell me about it, I'd love to hear about it.

Yours in fear, and fearlessness,

-Dan

subject: Take your opportunities seriously
content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "there" }},

Happy New Year!

I love that fresh-start-feeling that comes from a new calendar year. Don't you?

It helps me zoom out and think about my life and work with fresh eyes.

There's power and potential in taking the time for that kind of reflection. A new year offers so many opportunities. We should take them seriously!

Don't let this pass you by.

It can happen so quickly and easily. Days become weeks. Weeks become months. Months become years. And then too much time has slipped by.

If you're in a space where you're thinking about where you want to go, this is exactly what I created the Calling Course for — and for the next day it's open for new members.

What is the Calling Course? It's a distillation of 15+ years of study around psychology, career, story, personal formation, and personal development. It's the flagship offering of The Meaning Movement and only open for new members once or twice a year.

​Click here to see everything that's included along with a bunch of great bonuses I've gathered for anyone who joins this weekend: thecallingcourse.com/flash​

With using this material, I’ve seen people take action and take huge steps— even within the first few days of starting the course!

I would like to share a few of their stories.

As you read these stories, I invite you to imagine what a similar story from your future would sound like. What could your future self say if the tension was gone and you were at peace with your work?

Think about that, because that's what the Calling Course is here to do for you.

And if you haven't seen the other amazing stories, click here to see them!​

​

Finding Meaning without a Job Change

Elisabeth enjoyed her job, but always wondered if there was more for her out there. She questioned what her calling might be, but didn't know how to find answers.

In her words: "What if there is no dream job for me?"

As she began to unpack her story through the Calling Course, things shifted in a big way for her. She found freedom to explore and find meaning, purpose, and enjoyment in many of her different pursuits.

Back to her:

"The most valuable insight I got from The Calling Course was to dispel the myth that I have one singular "soulmate job" out there waiting for me.

Instead of solely focusing on the end result, Dan's guidance and the course helped me to engage in the foundational work of identifying where I find deep meaning and fulfillment."

Today she's still at her job, but enjoying the freedom and security it offers. She's finding more connection and purpose from it, which was a surprising. but welcomed outcome. She's also doubled down on her creative pursuits outside of work— most notably one that is becoming a small handmade goods company.

From unemployed to business consultant.

​

Joel is a dad in his 40’s who had pursued a few entrepreneurial ventures in the past, but his last one had just fallen apart on him. He was out of work and unsure what to do next. He felt like he was spinning his wheels. He didn’t want to end up in the same place he was before.

He wanted meaning, connection, movement, momentum. He wanted to find work that was uniquely his own.

Within the first weeks of digging into the course Joel emailed me and said, “I’m 3 modules into the course and already having some really good reflection… It’s really enjoyable and feel like I’m reconnecting to myself. I need to do more of that!”

He began to realize that his greatest gifts lie in helping teams become the best version of themselves. He began to connect the dots with his story and the work that he’s done and see how powerful and influential he can be when he’s working with teams.

As he strategized his next steps, he decided to launch a business consultancy to do his work and help teams. Today, he’s still growing it and loving it!

The course helped him overcome his fears, parse out what went wrong in his last endeavor, and identify what he really wants to do through his work.

After he finished the course he told me that it was exactly what he needed to get “traction again” and “stop spinning his wheels”.

I love these stories JUST. SO. MUCH! They make me feel so grateful that I get to be a part of this work! And I’d love for your story to be the next one I tell.

Registration for the The Calling Course Closes tomorrow, and I don't want you to miss it.

​Click here to see everything that’s included.

This is the proven program to walk you step-by-step through finding purpose, meaning, fulfillment in your work and life. There’s nothing else quite like it out there.

I’d love to have you join.

​Click here to see the details.​

See you there,

-Dan

PPS - If you haven't checked out everything I've prepared for you with the course, click here to see it. It's only available until tomorrow night.​

subject: Creating Your Path, Pursuing Dual Careers, Meeting Oprah, and Making Belief with Calvin Nowell
preview_text: What if you switch jobs too often?  What if you don't love your work, but you've recently made a change?  How many transitions are too many? And more!
content:
{% if subscriber.first_name != blank %}
Hello {{ subscriber.first_name }},
{% else %}
Hello,
{% endif %}

So many of us have multiple passions that compete for time, attention, and resources — especially when it comes to our careers and work. So often we feel the need to choose one thing and leave behind all the rest in order to excel and succeed.

But what if you don't actually have to choose? What if you can be successful at more than one pursuit at that same time?

This is a question I often ask myself. If you've listened to the show for some time, you'll know that's true about me.

Culture tends to push us toward the myth that we can only do one thing to be successful. And while there is a trade off involved in multiple pursuits, there's also a synergy that can be present between projects.

Our guest today demonstrates that well. Calvin Nowell is both a singer and marketer. He pursues both in tandem as two parallel careers.

We get into his story, why he does what he does, how he got to meet Oprah, and so many other fantastic things.

So let's dive into it.

subject: Friday Favorites
content:
Hi Meanies!

Happy Friday! From time to time I like to take stock of the things in my life that are especially fun and share them with you. Here's my short list for the week. I'd love to hear yours!

What I'm enjoying right now:
​​
​Bluey (kids TV show) - My family has been really enjoying this show on Disney+. It's about a family of Australian cattle dogs. These dogs are continuously a role model of fun, light-hearted, and connected parenting. My favorite episode so far is Bike, which is about failure and developing grit. It made me cry. If you have kids, I encourage you to dance to the intro music with them.

Stillwater (kids tv show) - This is a show about a family that lives next door to a panda on Apple TV. It teaches mindfulness and how to deal with big emotions — something that my family and I always need reminders of. It's slow paced and real.

Magic Spoon (fun cereal for adults) - My wife bought me a few boxes of this amazing cereal. I enjoy into eating well and healthy and love having a treat that fits in my fitness nutrition macros. Plus the branding and design is really fun. If kids cereals without the sugar sound interesting, this is for you. So far the "Fruity" flavor is my favorite. It tastes like Frootloops. Yummmm.

​Miroco Kettle (coffee/tea kettle) - My wife also bought me a new kettle for making coffee and tea at home. It's pretty, well balanced, and can hold your water at just the right temperature for whatever you're brewing. It makes me happy every time I use it — and I use it 2+ times a day!

​Simple exercise bands (fitness equipment) - This is fitness-geek-ish, but I bought a set of these to keep me working out while traveling, and have used them every day since. Life with small kids and multiple businesses leaves me short on time for workouts. These allow me to squeeze in some extra movements here and there between other activities. It's my current workout secret sauce.

What's on your Friday Favorites list? I'd love to know what you're enjoying in life right now!

-Dan

subject: Finding Your Edge with Laura Huang
content:

Laura Huang is a researcher and professor at Harvard Business School. She researches and teaches on concepts of perception and bias in work and business.

Her work has been featured in all kinds of impressive places: The Wall Street Journal, Forbes, and a whole bunch of others.

Through her work Laura helps people come to understand how others see them, take control of that narrative, and use it to their advantage.

subject: How should I end this?
content:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "friends" }},

It's the end of the year. This brings a valuable opportunity to reflect and reset.

And boy do we need it this year.

It’s tempting to flip the calendar to 2021 without thinking back about 2020, but it’s more important than ever not to move ahead to quickly.

If you're anything like me, I can hardly remember the start of 2020. It’s uniquely vague, unlike most years.

(Granted, my wife and I had a baby in the middle of the year, and combined with the other two kids we already had — I haven’t gotten as much sleep this year as I would have liked.)

My sleep and parenting struggles aside, 2020 is a year that has changed a lot for many people.

And it’s important to take note.

Many of us had work situations change in 2020.

Many of us had social situations change in 2020.

Many of us stayed home a lot in 2020.

Many of us had more time on our hands in 2020.

Many of us had less time on our hands in 2020.

Many of us lost a loved one in 2020.

Let’s not let these changes pass us by without reflection.

2021 may or may not bring about a better world — I hope it does! But no matter what, you won't won't be able to create a future that you want to create unless you understand where you've been.

As we change calendar years, there is tremendous value is doing two things: looking back and looking forward.

Some years ago I created an Annual Review guide to help with this process. It walks you through a process of pausing, reflecting, evaluating, and goal setting.

It’s free. I hope you’ll take some time to do it along with me.

​Click here to get it: https://themeaningmovement.com/annual-review/​

This year more than any other.

See you next year,

-Dan

When it comes to finding your calling, the best way forward is step-by-step guidance.

Sure, you can figure it out on your own if you have the time (hours spent on trial and error, reading books, going to conferences, meeting with coaches, etc.) and the money (coaches and conferences cost a lot!).

But why do that if you don’t have to?

You don’t have to wander and hope that you’re making progress if you don’t want to. I’ve tried that before. It doesn’t work very well.

With the Calling Course, I’ve seen people take action and take huge steps— even within the first few days of starting the course!

As you read these stories, I invite you to imagine what a similar story from your future would sound like. What could your future self say if the tension was gone and you were at peace with your work?

Think about that, because that's what the Calling Course is here to do for you.

And if you haven't seen the other amazing stories, click here to see them!​

From caring for customers to caring for souls

When Kelsey started the process, she was making good money working in customer service and sales. She was good at what she did, but felt like something was missing.

As she dug into the material, she began to connect some of the dots and accept that she’s incredibly gifted at caring for people on a spiritual level. For a number of reasons, she had been avoiding that truth about herself for quite some time. There was a lot of pain and heartbreak that made her afraid of that part of herself and her story.

Through the course she was able to see how strong she was in that area, and how moving it is when she gets to be a part of a person’s spiritual development.

Today, Kelsey is a pastor and therapist.

​

Finding Meaning without a Job Change

​

Elisabeth enjoyed her job, but always wondered if there was more for her out there. She questioned what her calling might be, but didn't know how to find answers.

In her words: "What if there is no dream job for me?"

As she began to unpack her story through the Calling Course, things shifted in a big way for her. She found freedom to explore and find meaning, purpose, and enjoyment in many of her different pursuits.

Back to her:

"The most valuable insight I got from The Calling Course was to dispel the myth that I have one singular "soulmate job" out there waiting for me.

Instead of solely focusing on the end result, Dan's guidance and the course helped me to engage in the foundational work of identifying where I find deep meaning and fulfillment."

Today she's still at her job, but enjoying the freedom and security it offers. She's finding more connection and purpose from it, which was a surprising. but welcomed outcome. She's also doubled down on her creative pursuits outside of work— most notably one that is becoming a small handmade goods company.

From unemployed to business consultant.

​

Joel is a dad in his 40’s who had pursued a few entrepreneurial ventures in the past, but his last one had just fallen apart on him. He was out of work and unsure what to do next. He felt like he was spinning his wheels. He didn’t want to end up in the same place he was before.

He wanted meaning, connection, movement, momentum. He wanted to find work that was uniquely his own.

Within the first weeks of digging into the course Joel emailed me and said, “I’m 3 modules into the course and already having some really good reflection… It’s really enjoyable and feel like I’m reconnecting to myself. I need to do more of that!”

He began to realize that his greatest gifts lie in helping teams become the best version of themselves. He began to connect the dots with his story and the work that he’s done and see how powerful and influential he can be when he’s working with teams.

As he strategized his next steps, he decided to launch a business consultancy to do his work and help teams. Today, he’s still growing it and loving it!

The course helped him overcome his fears, parse out what went wrong in his last endeavor, and identify what he really wants to do through his work.

After he finished the course he told me that it was exactly what he needed to get “traction again” and “stop spinning his wheels”.

I love these stories JUST. SO. MUCH! They make me feel so grateful that I get to be a part of this work! And I’d love for your story to be the next one I tell.

Registration for the The Calling Course Closes tomorrow, and I don't want you to miss it.

This is the proven program to walk you step-by-step through finding purpose, meaning, fulfillment in your work and life. There’s nothing else quite like it out there.

See you there,

-Dan

subject: Name your fear (response requested!)
content:
Hi Meanies,

I was just in your inbox with the first video in this 3 part masterclass. I'm LOVING the replies that I'm getting! Keep them coming!

But I'm visiting your inbox fagain, because I need to get real with you.

I remember feeling REALLY stuck. I didn’t know what to do with my life. I had been working a job for a long time that didn’t fit but I stayed in it because I thought it was what I was “supposed to do” based on my degree, disposition, gender, experience, and others’ expectations of me. All these things contributed to a mindset that kept me in this job far too long – eventually negatively impacting my mental and physical health, and my family life as well.

Deep down, if I really listened, I knew I needed to identify and find something different. But, I didn’t know what, or how, or if I was good enough. I was dominated by fear.

Fearful of putting all my effort into a business plan or job application that may not pan out.

Fearful of being told I was “asking too much” for my life.

Fearful of being judged by my friends and family.

Fearful of wanting a role that didn’t yet exist.

Fearful of letting people down.

Ultimately what I ended up fearing the most was this: things staying the same.

What would happen to my life if I stayed in this job? Would I be happy, or wake up years later a miserable human?

With that, I challenge you to begin this journey by naming your own fears. Take a moment and identify your fears and beliefs that hold you back from giving this aspect of your life the attention and consideration it deserves.

There are no right or wrong answers; only your truth. I'll read every response and do my best to keep up with replies.

Onward Meanies!

- Dan

PS- I really do want to hear from you. What are your biggest fears about finding your calling/purpose/meaning? Hit reply and let me know! I read every email.

Nick Cox has done some deep work around calling and vocation in his life. I loved this interview because we were able to go places that many guests just aren't ready to go. Which is to say, you can tell Nick has done his work.
​
He's also a good friend and long time listener of the Meaning Movement and member of the Calling Course, so I've had the privilege of getting glimpses of his process along the way.
​
Nick's tired of the common narrative of quitting your day job and doing what you love as the primary way to purpose and meaning, which is why we decided to do this interview. He's representative of a demographic that I tend to miss with my guests, those who are taking a less entrepreneurial path.
​
This conversation goes from discussing the high level philosophy of calling to deep into Nick's story pretty quickly. Spoiler alert, it gets a bit emotional at some points.
​
But I also think this is one of the most important conversations that I've had the opportunity to share on the podcast, simply because of who Nick is and the perspective that he brings to the conversation.

I hope you enjoy this as much as I did speaking with him. It's a powerful conversation. And if you find it impactful, I'd love for you to share it with anyone who may benefit.

subject: Understanding Your Motivation
content:
{% if subscriber.first_name != blank %}
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name }},
{% else %}
Hi Friends,

Have you ever needed and wanted to do something, but struggled to get into action to get it done?

When I look at the way my energy for activities shifts— it can seem so illogical. There are things that I can't wait to get out of bed to do, and there are other things that I can't get myself out of bed to do.​
​
​Why is that?​
​
​Today on the podcast, we get to dig in and attempt to answer that question. My guest today is Todd Henry — author, podcaster, and creative director. He's the founder of the Accidental Creative podcast — a show that has more than a million downloads. He's also the author of a handful of books, including his most recent: the Motivation Code.​
​
​I really enjoyed my conversation with Todd for many reasons. He's a great conversation partner and knowledgeable in all the areas I enjoy: creativity, psychology, business, and more.​
​
​We dive into his work journey, and his new book. You'll have some good take aways for your own work and life, including a better understanding of how you're motivated and how to use that to your advantage.​

subject: Is Time Flexible?
content:
{% if subscriber.first_name != blank %}
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name }},

Hi Friends,

Time is a strange thing. Though it always continues on, it sometimes feels as though it moves quickly and other times slowly.​
​
In work, sometimes it's easy to manage our time and what we can fit into a few hours or a day. Other times it gets away from us — leaving us frustrated and unsatisfied.​
​
​These are some of the attributes of time that fascinate Laura Vanderkam and drew her to build a career out of writing on the topic.​
​
​Laura is the bestselling author of What the Most Successful People Do Before Breakfast, I Know How She Does It, 168 Hours, among others. She is the host of a few podcasts and her work has appeared in The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, Fast Company, Fortune, and other publications.​
​
​I really enjoyed speaking with Laura about her new book, as well as many different aspects of time and time management. I hope you will as well.​
​

Hi Meanies,

While days seem to blur together right now due to the pandemic, I know these past few days will be remembered forever… forever… forever… for...ev...er...

***a harp plays as I imagine the future***

Me, as an old man: Gather round children. Let me tell you about the time when I ran a crazy sale for my 38th birthday!

Grandchildren: Grandpa Dan! We know! The Great Flash Sale of 2020. You’ve told us a million times!

Me: Oh yes. That was so crazy! Let me tell it to you again…

subject: Your Ticket to Freedom 🚀
content:
{% if subscriber.first_name != blank %}
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name }},
{% else %}
Hi Friends,
{% endif %}

I remember feeling really stuck. I didn’t know what to do with my life. I had been working a job that didn’t fit. I thought it was what I was “supposed to do” (more on that ahead). I wanted to find something different, but I didn’t know what to try. I was alone.

I was afraid.

Afraid of putting all my effort into something that didn’t pan out.

Afraid of disappointing friends and family.

Afraid of not being able to have an impressive answer to that dreaded question: “so… what do you do?”

Afraid of wanting something that didn’t exist.

I could go on and on.

It’s because of this experience that I created the Calling Course. It’s what I wish I’d had years ago to get me through.

For the next two days, you can get access to the Calling Course for 50% off the normal price. I’ve never done a discount before, but there’s a lot happening in the world that we haven’t seen before. I want to help. And so this is your chance.

Check it out here: https://thecallingcourse.com/flash-sale

What I know now is that there's a difference between doing what you're made to do and doing what you're "supposed to do". I knew it then too, but I didn't have the words for it. Many of us end up doing the "supposed to's" while thinking it's what we're meant to do.

And for good reason! We all have internalized expectations that we're constantly navigating. It's really hard to hear ourselves in the midst of them.

But also, many of those expectations are good and helpful, so you can't just abandon them.

All of which adds up to a really big pile of stuck. Stuck between what we want to do and what we need to do. It's a mess!

While most people would find working their way through that mess tedious and painful — I LOVE it! It's so fun to help people find freedom in the midst of all of that.

After developing my process for years and workshopping it constantly, I build The Calling Course around it so anyone can access it and find that sense of freedom.

If you're ready to get unstuck, land your dream job, or otherwise find your next big thing, click here to join us: https://thecallingcourse.com/flash-sale

You won't be disappointed.

See you there,

-Dan

Work is changing. This isn't new, but the pace has increased exponentially. While on the surface there's a lot of conversation about the pandemic, social distancing, quarantine, and when all of this will end, below the surface shifts are taking place.

More people are working from home than ever before (maybe you're one of them?).

More people are out of work than ever before (maybe also you're one of them?).

  • 🎥 Video Speed Controller - I watch a lot of videos to get information quickly. This plugin allows you to control the speed. It's best to use with a keyboard shortcut so you can quickly speed up and slow down a video to get to the content that you want and need.

  • 📚Library Extension - I read a lot (56 books last year), so I'm always looking out for my next book. This extension connects with your local library database and allows you to look up and place a hold right from sites like Amazon or Goodreads. Though my local libraries are closed right now, there's still a lot of digital content that I can find and access. Also, if you use Goodreads, connect with me here.

That's all for now. Any favorites that you use?

Stay safe and sane out there.

subject: Calling all Teachers and Helping Professionals!
content:
Hi friends,

I believe in teachers and people who dedicate their lives to helping professions. As many of you know, I was a youth pastor for 5 crazy years!

But there's something unique that can happen when you're in one of those jobs. You start because you want to change the world. It's hard, but you know it's worth it. You're doing it because it means something to you!

But because of the load that’s put on your shoulders and the lack of resources available to support you — more and more people are finding themselves burnt out and needing to leave.

So what do you do next… when the thing you loved no longer works for you?

That’s the exact question my friend and former teacher Brittany set out to answer.

Today she’s a six-figure freelancer and entrepreneur, but even more important to her than that -- she’s helping teachers find meaning again through their work.

She’s helping teachers that feel burnt out and frustrated -- on their last straw -- figure out what to do next.

She’s helping teachers that love teaching but just need help making ends meet figure out how to do that.

And she’s sharing all of her knowledge in the FREE More than Teachers Summit. You’ll hear from other former teachers on what they’re doing now, how they made that transition, and tips in case that career path interests you, too.

Though helping teachers is her thing, the same ideas apply to all helping professionals, and anyone who needs to make a change, in fact. You’ll hear from others that weren’t teachers but are helping people find what’s next— including yours truly! And I can't wait for you to watch the training I did with Britney! It was a blast!

If you’re looking for more meaning and not finding it anymore from teaching -- or have found meaning but you need a way to pay the bills through something on the side -- you’ll want to be at the virtual More than Teachers Summit.

It starts on tomorrow. Access is FREE. So jump in now: http://themeaningmovement.com/more-than-teachers

See you in there!

Dan
